title: Inference Hinting Garden — scratch journal
content:
Context / motivation:
- We're good at routing by model/region/capacity but apps often know higher-level intent that the runtime doesn't: user intent (urgent vs leisurely), content-sensitivity, content-length expectation, revenue-signal, and display constraints (e.g., mobile preview).
- If callers could send lightweight, structured hints about these dimensions, the runtime could make smarter choices: pick cheaper quantized variant, favor low-latency instance, apply prefix caching differently, or trigger a graceful degrade path.

What is an "inference hint"?
- Small, explicit metadata fields attached to requests (not full policy config) that express preferences or constraints.
- Should be low-cost to add from client side, optional, and backward-compatible. Runtime treats hints as advisory (soft) unless customer opts-in to strict SLO bindings.

Hypothesis: A minimal set of hints will let us reduce per-token cost by ~10–30% on heterogeneous workloads while keeping user-facing latency within SLOs and improving graceful fallbacks.

Candidate hint dimensions (brainstorm):
- priority: low | normal | high  -> prefer batching/cost vs latency
- fidelity: preview | standard | canonical -> choose model size/quantization level or re-rank step
- deadline_ms: integer -> hard/soft latency target (for scheduling/burst routing)
- revenue_signal: zero | low | medium | high -> trade cost for quality on higher ARPU flows
- privacy_level: public | pii | pii-encrypted -> route to Private/Dedicated when needed
- partial_responses_allowed: yes | no -> enable chunked streaming or early-stop
- size_hint: short | medium | long -> influence context window tuning and KV cache usage
- user_affinity: warm | cold -> if warm, attempt to use cached KV/prefix; if cold, prefer fast cold-start nodes
- fallback_strategy: auto_fallback | no_fallback | degrade_to_summary -> controls graceful degrade behavior

API sketch (lightweight, v0):
- HTTP header or JSON envelope field: "x-redwood-hints" or "hints": {..}
- Example request envelope: {
  "input": "Summarize this long thread...",
  "hints": {"priority":"low","fidelity":"preview","deadline_ms":3000}
}
- Service-level behavior: runtime reads hints, maps to routing policy, and logs a hint-usage metric. Hints are not enforced unless user's workspace toggles "hint-strict".

User stories
- PM (B2B chat app): "When generating message previews we want cheaper outputs fast; we add fidelity=preview so costs stay low for millions of previews."
- Platform engineer: "Route pii content to Private cluster when privacy_level=pii instead of relying on token-scanning."
- Growth engineer: "Mark onboarding emails as high revenue_signal so we bias higher-quality models for conversion flows."
- Mobile UX: "When size_hint=short we can use a compact UI and lower token window so mobile latency improves."

Operational safety and telemetry
- Need a new set of metrics: hint uptake, hint->actual routing decisions, cost delta per hint, quality regressions by hint bucket.
- A/B experiment: sample X% requests with hints active vs disabled to measure regression risk.
- Audit trail: store hint metadata in request logs for compliance; surface in Console with rollup charts.

Experiments to run (MVP):
1) preview fidelity experiment for the "preview" use case (e.g., search result snippets).
   - Implement mapping: fidelity=preview -> use 6-bit quantized model and aggressive early-stop; compare quality vs baseline.
2) deadline_ms scheduling: enforce soft deadlines and measure tail-latency reductions and cost tradeoffs.
3) privacy_level routing: hook hint into Private routing to reduce false positives from content classification.
4) revenue-signal gating: for high revenue calls route to dedicated capacity and measure conversion uplift (internal only).

Acceptance criteria for MVP
- API: caller can attach hints with <3ms overhead and no breaking changes.
- Runtime: hints result in different routing / model selection at least 80% of the time for mapped rules.
- Telemetry: we capture metrics and can show cost delta and P50/P95 latency per hint bucket.
- Safety: no >2% quality regression for critical flows during canary.

Implementation notes / quick tech sketch
- Mapping layer sits in the ingress router (before batching) so the decision influences queueing/batching behavior.
- Bring your own mapping rules (config per-customer) vs default global policy. Start with safe, narrow defaults.
- Persist hints in tracing spans for downstream observability.
- Consider adding hint-aggregator in Console to allow product folks to see distributions and tune mappings.

Open questions / risks
- Will product teams overuse hints and create fragmentation? Need sane defaults and quotas.
- How to prevent gaming revenue_signal? (fraud detection / authenticated signals)
- Privacy: hints could leak internal signals — treat hints as metadata with retention and RBAC policies.
- Compliance: tying privacy_level to routing must be auditable and provable.

Next steps / TODOs
- [ ] Rapid proto: header-based v0 that maps fidelity=preview -> model-x-6bit and priority=low -> batch-friendly queue. (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Design dashboard view for hint telemetry (owner: Lena)
- [ ] Draft docs: minimal API spec, examples, and backward-compat story (owner: Sam)
- [ ] Create JIRA spike to measure cost delta on 3 internal workloads (owner: team)
- [ ] Run small canary with 2 internal apps and collect quality metrics for 2 weeks.

Notes to self: keep this lean. Hints should be helpful, not another knobs page. Start opinionated, then build config surface. Also check with legal about whether "privacy_level" needs explicit customer consent in contracts.

References / inspiration:
- internal: confluence/INF-HINTS-ideas (linked above)
- academic: "importance-aware scheduling for batch inference" (paper notes in repo)
- competitor: observed systems that use "quality tags" at request time (no public API I could find)

Random brainwave: what if hints could be learned? App sends a few labeled examples (implicit feedback over time), and the platform suggests hint mappings automatically (e.g., these patterns are usually low-fidelity safe). Long-term but worth noting.

End of pad.
summary: Personal scratchpad exploring a lightweight 'inference hints' idea: request-level metadata to guide runtime routing and model selection. Includes candidate hint dimensions, API sketch, user stories, MVP experiments, metrics, open questions, and next steps.
